method: Manual normative review, compiler/runtime inspection, and MLIR regression evidence. This inventory is not a full conformance certification.
z3: Pinned in-process Z3 4.13.4 for compiler bit-vector planning, ordinary runtime residual completion and exact integral sampling; native and WASM target libraries are statically merged into simulator runtime archives.

features.detail: Every numbered subsection is represented; open implementation items remain explicit.
Reviewed against compiler preparation, generated checkers, and runtime search.

Compiler Z3 proves static plans. Native and WASM runtime Z3 complete ordinary and explicitly ordered packed integral residuals of arbitrary aggregate width with live captures, frozen bits, domains, block masks and optimal soft priorities. Weighted and runtime-foreach paths retain limits; non-integral forms remain incomplete.
Commit occurs only on a successful solve; pre_randomize side effects are independently observable.

Exact compiler Z3 plans and tables are uniform. Ordinary native/WASM integral residuals now use Z3-proven sparse component tables or exact Boolean model counts and arbitrary-precision rejection-sampled ranks, including live captures, frozen bits, domains, block masks and optimal soft priorities. Runtime foreach, non-integral forms and other explicitly partial paths remain open.
Packed integer domains and arbitrary-width rand bit vectors are executable.

Named enumerators, anonymous and typedef inventories are frozen before AST disposal. Representations through 64 bits are admitted; colliding semantic display names with different source domains are diagnosed rather than conflated.
Entire packed bit patterns are legal; nested enum members do not restrict the aggregate domain.
The LRM disallows rand and randc packed tagged unions; frontend validation applies to source declarations. Legacy synthetic IR domain support is not a language feature.

features.feature: Unpacked arrays, queues, and associative arrays
features.detail: Fixed unpacked arrays of packed integral elements use exact logical bitstreams for class and scope randomization, including multidimensional, descending, ascending and negative ranges. Enum domains apply independently to each element. One-dimensional dynamic arrays and queues retain specialized plans. Per-element randc histories and modes, non-integral leaves, general indexed constraints and associative arrays remain incomplete.

features.feature: Unpacked structs with member rand qualifiers
features.detail: The executable property planner currently requires packed values or admitted dynamic containers and class handles.
1800-2023 real constraints require real-valued solver domains; current serialized solver is bit-vector only.
Finite acyclic type graphs, polymorphism, aliases, nulls, and descendant constraints are supported; recursive type graphs remain incomplete.
Values may repeat; enabled properties are committed together.
Shared class storage and shared mode state are planned.
Integral semantic domains up to 2^32 values and 32-bit representation use a keyed bijection.
A single randc property skips rejected values and restarts cycles; joint randc and rand properties need further cycle-domain review.
Each property has cycle state; the full LRM joint solvability and restart behavior needs dedicated coverage.

features.feature: Randc real and dist on randc
features.detail: Forbidden by the language; existing diagnostics cover dist and width restrictions.
Total packed expressions, arithmetic, bitwise operators, inside, concatenation, constant replication, and conditional expressions are compiled to MLIR and solver programs.
Division needs a known nonzero divisor; dynamic signed exponents and general system functions are not admitted.
Effective block inventories and individual mode bits are preserved.
Resolved extern bodies participate in Z3 planning, reusable templates, effective inherited constraints, and generated native/bytecode checking.
An implicit prototype without a body is treated as an empty constraint, as required by 18.5.1.
An explicit extern block without a resolved body is diagnosed. Effective pure declarations require a concrete implementation.
Base-first class inventories apply effective overrides and the 2023 extends marker.

features.feature: Soft priorities across inherited and contained objects
features.detail: Derived and inline priorities are handled; all cross-object ordering cases need verification.
Constant integral endpoints, explicit weights, default ranges, and additive overlapping items have executable plans.
Self-determined integral weights are zero-extended, including negative signed bit patterns.

Runtime Z3 preserves each constant integral item's original mass after filtering. Exact target projections and arbitrary-precision normalization support wide weights, overlapping items and noncontiguous defaults. Expression targets, dynamic endpoints and real ranges remain open.

features.feature: Nonzero weights never make an otherwise legal solve fail
features.detail: The runtime Z3 policy removes 64-bit mass overflow and bounded-domain traversal failures for admitted fixed integral distributions; full 2^64 ranges and arbitrary-width unsigned captures are covered. General expression targets, unresolved activation and function-priority stage combinations remain diagnosed.

features.feature: Soft dist and dist with solve before
features.detail: Runtime Z3 retains or discards soft distributions in global soft-priority order and samples whole distributed targets conditionally on earlier solve-before layers. State guards and earlier candidate guards are supported. Split-target ordering, unresolved candidate activation and independent function-priority stage combinations remain open.

features.feature: Multiple active distributions on one target
features.detail: Runtime Z3 combines per-value masses from every enabled distribution on admitted direct integral targets, preserving legal intersections even for incompatible requested marginals. General expression targets and real distributions remain open.

features.feature: Dynamic endpoints, candidate weights, and real ranges
features.detail: Require a generalized distribution planner and real domains.

Integral singular values and fixed unpacked arrays or slices expand into pairwise leaf inequality before Z3 planning. Multidimensional arrays, ascending and negative bounds, fixed state-array leaves, singleton groups, and duplicate references are covered in class and scope randomization. Duplicate leaves retain their identity and make the solve fail. Real leaves and dynamically sized container operands remain incomplete.
Packed two-state implication is present in Z3 and residual programs, including soft guards.
Hard and guarded soft constraints retain conditional semantics.
Fixed foreach dimensions expand into ordinary predicates before Z3 planning and function dependency analysis; runtime iteration covers admitted one-dimensional dynamic arrays and queues.
Live size, declared iterator type, universal conjunction, and empty-array identity are implemented.

features.feature: Fixed, associative, string, and multidimensional foreach
features.detail: Fixed packed and unpacked dimensions, including multidimensional arrays, descending or negative bounds and omitted iterators, expand into typed constant-index predicates for class and scope randomization. Fixed state-array elements are captured per predicate. Z3 handles the resulting ordinary relation, live modes, soft preferences and explicit solve-before on integral elements. Associative, string, non-integral leaves and generalized runtime dimensions remain incomplete.

Fixed foreach is expanded before planning, and state FALSE/TRUE guards suppress known invalid array accesses through the full Figure 18-3 algebra. Runtime state bounds include signed, wide and unknown indices. Complete runtime-sized candidate solving remains open.
Selected dynamic array and queue reductions are lowered; all containers, methods, and with expressions are not covered.
Finite acyclic object graphs solve together with alias deduplication; arbitrary recursive graphs and object arrays remain open.
Self edges and cycles are diagnosed; aliases and packed paths retain precise ordering masks.

Compiler Z3 tables and structural plans preserve ordering with arbitrary-width masks and projected keys. Native and WASM runtime Z3 count exact existential projections for integral bitstreams, including live captures, semantic domains, modes and optimal soft preferences; each projected value counts once regardless of its later completions. Version-2 ordering metadata carries multiword masks. Compiler and runtime DAG plans defer partially ordered fields to their latest legal layer and include unordered fields in the final joint group. Fixed integral array elements use the same exact masks and conditional probabilities; whole unpacked arrays and randc operands are diagnosed. Real ordering and state-dependent selected paths remain incomplete.
Randc candidates are fixed before ordinary rand solving; combined cyclic solvability needs broader coverage.
Class-wide storage is shared by every instance and inherited plans use the same storage.
Expression returns, blocking result assignments, nested calls, and virtual receiver dispatch are supported; procedural control flow and other receivers are incomplete.
Random properties read only inside a function are frozen as pre-solve state; argument paths remain solver variables.

features.feature: Implicit function priority can shrink solution space
features.detail: Native and WASM target Z3 solve higher-only integral constraint sets independently, freeze accepted arguments, and allow lower stages to fail without committing assignments or solver RNG. Source path masks preserve syntactic dependencies through simplification; guarded atoms retain separate stages. Explicit solve-before uses conditional projections within each function stage. Wide packed paths, soft priorities, live modes, frozen arguments and semantic domains are covered. Staged randc histories, aliased object identity, dynamic foreach and general procedural function evaluation remain open and are diagnosed.

Signedness casts, clog2, countones, onehot, onehot0, and countbits lower to the same unsigned bit-vector operations in Z3, native, WASM, and narrow/wide residual programs. Candidate bits are two-state; mixed unknown-plane captures and other system functions remain open.

Scope randomization shares class expression-function validation, packed path priority analysis and target Z3 stages. Module/package and other non-instance expression functions support nested calls, actual-argument priority, frozen body state reads, output/ref restrictions, cycle diagnostics, and wide integral assignments. Instance receiver plans, procedural control flow and general function bodies remain incomplete.
Integral state predicates and handle comparisons are evaluated safely before solving, including null and bounds checks. Mixed unknown-plane predicates and non-integral solving remain open.

The complete Figure 18-3 truth tables are implemented with safe compiler captures and hard creation-validity predicates in native and WASM solving. Only state TRUE/FALSE suppress errors; RANDOM cannot hide them. Null handles, handle comparisons, fixed/state dynamic array and queue bounds, known invalid random-array slices, state tagged-union arms, guarded body errors, disabled blocks and frozen variables are covered. Unused function inputs retain evaluation errors and source RANDOM classification. Live guard reference and argument masks preserve independent Z3 function-priority stages after sifting. General candidate-dependent accesses, unknown-plane mixtures and complete runtime-sized foreach encoding remain open.
Up to 64 preferences use lexicographic satisfiability in Z3 and residual evaluation.
Guards belong to the predicate while target reference collection examines the soft expression itself.
Later declaration, derived class, and inline preferences receive higher priority.

Static foreach expansion preserves declaration-order iteration so later body instances receive higher soft priority, including descending ranges. Full object-containment and runtime-iteration relationships still need coverage.

Direct identifiers and fixed integral paths discard only earlier directly referencing preferences, including unused function inputs. Enclosing guards and indirect function body reads do not trigger a disable.

features.feature: Live block modes and conditional disable
features.detail: The generated checker and narrow/wide runtime programs honor block masks and if/implication guards; Z3 uses the all-enabled planning state.
Derived and inline preferences after a disable remain active.
Dynamic selections, unpacked paths, and foreach disable targets are not covered by the fixed path matcher.
Randomize and hook plans dispatch through the concrete class selected for a handle.

features.feature: Randomize return status and atomic property commit
features.detail: Successful solves return one; failed or null-receiver calls return zero without property commits.
Ordinary draws work; randc behavior with arbitrary cycle-domain changes needs additional tests.
Pre runs before state capture; post runs after a successful commit and is skipped on failure; graph aliases invoke hooks once.
Finite graphs are supported; recursive and generalized container graphs are incomplete.
Effective constraints, properties, and hooks are resolved against the selected concrete class.

features.feature: Inline constraints merge with class constraints
features.detail: Inline hard constraints intersect the effective class formula; inline soft preferences have higher priority.
Frozen lookup inventories distinguish randomized receiver members from enclosing scope captures.
Frontend bindings preserve local:: and enclosing lexical scope through constraint preparation.
Queries and setters retain mode state; disabled variables are fixed and not committed.

Fixed unpacked integral arrays have persistent per-leaf mode bitmaps, including multidimensional subarray setters, arbitrary leaf counts, static sharing, and inherited dynamic-class resets. Disabled four-state leaves preserve X/Z on commits. Only singular leaves may be queried. Dynamic arrays, queues, and per-element randc histories remain open.

With runtime Z3, finite integral partial selections use exact projected counts with frozen bits, including sparse wide constraints and fixed array element masks. The optional no-runtime-Z3 fallback remains bounded; non-integral and dynamic-container relations remain open.
Masks control hard/soft predicates and ordering edges; disable-soft uses the live mask too.
Mode-sensitive residual checks are correct within their bounded domain, but capture-free proofs do not remove general runtime completeness limits.
State captures are evaluated for each call; mode masks select the live formula.
General joint cycle-domain invalidation remains open.
Listed non-rand values become random temporarily; unlisted properties remain state; persistent mode state is preserved.
Packed values and static fields work; non-packed selected values retain planner restrictions.
Hooks and constraint checks run on current values, with no random draws or property writes; post runs only on success.
Up to 64 automatic, formal, static, package, and design values can be selected.
Packed integral, enum, and packed aggregates work; dynamic containers, class handles, and non-packed types remain incomplete.
Variables and the process stream are committed only when the solve succeeds.

sections.title: Adding constraints to scope variables—std::randomize() with

features.feature: Scope with constraints and zero arguments
features.detail: State captures, hard/soft constraints, disable-soft, and current-state checking use the same solver plan.
Fixed member offsets are encoded as logical extraction in Z3 and the residual program.
Direct ordering works within finite limits; user function plans and general selected paths are incomplete.

sections.title: Random number system functions and methods

features.feature: Process and object random API family
features.detail: PCG state and bounded draws have native and bytecode implementations.

features.feature: Urandom unsigned return and optional seed
features.detail: $urandom supports zero arguments and an optional integral seed. Explicit seeding replaces both PCG state words with the same canonical mapping as process::srandom, so equal seeds determine equal sequences across independently inherited thread streams, including negative 32-bit seeds and repeated seeding.
One or two bounds, reversed bounds, and full-width endpoints use rejection debiasing.
Manual reseeding preserves stream independence and does not draw a value.
Exact object and process RNG snapshots are serialized.
Restores exact snapshots and future stream output.

Scope initialization streams, static and dynamic process streams, and object streams are independent. Lexical module/interface/program/package ownership is preserved through native and bytecode startup.

features.feature: Independent initialization RNG for each scope instance
features.detail: Each module/interface/program/package semantic owner has a distinct RNG seeded with the configured default. Static initializers and process registration resume that stream; optional $urandom(seed) arguments remain supported.
Processes and objects have explicit independent state.
Forked processes and bytecode tasks split the parent stream in lexical creation order.
Root-spawned static processes split their declaring scope initialization RNG independently of unrelated scopes; dynamic children still split their running parent.
New objects split the creator stream; object copying creates a reseeded stream.
Synchronous static declaration initializers bind their lexical initialization RNG with no active logical thread. Class creation consumes that stream directly before static processes are created.
Object and process srandom plus snapshots allow deterministic replay.
Each weight is evaluated once; summation uses maximum operand precision with modular overflow.
No branch and no RNG draw occur when the total is zero.
Weights through 64 bits are executable; arbitrary-width bounded sampling is not implemented.
Finite void grammars are frozen into MLIR; recursive grammars and value passing remain incomplete.
Unspecified weights are one and explicit integral weights are evaluated on production entry.
Current finite grammar arithmetic requires further overflow and negative-weight diagnostic review.
Finite grammar production conditionals lower to control flow.
First matching case and default rules are represented in finite production control flow.
Repeat counts and loop control are represented in the frozen grammar.
Current support covers shallow finite production items; generalized nested interleaving and bias remain incomplete.
Void grammar abort control is supported; value-returning production aborts require value-passing support.
The runtime grammar slice only admits void, parameter-free productions.
